title: Asset and Debt
premise: Edmund Nystrom — born Anya Volkova, living as a man under his fourth identity — is a former intelligence analyst turned whistle-blower hiding in a Lisbon safehouse when a passenger flight he helped manifest vanishes from every radar, manifest, and database while still airborne. The plane lands anyway, carrying a defector named Ilse Brandt who carries proof that Edmund's old agency manufactured the 'incident' that destroyed his life and killed the family that took him in. Hunted by the agency's fixer and unable to trust the journalist network that once saved him, Edmund must smuggle Ilse to the Geneva summit where her evidence goes public — realizing only at the border that Ilse herself may be the bait designed to flush out every ghost the agency ever created. Edmund chooses to walk her into the trap anyway, trading his last clean identity for hers, and in the aftermath, the found family he thought he'd lost claims him under a fifth name — one he chose himself.
about_author: Mirabel Quintana is the pen name of a former shipping-logistics analyst who writes thrillers about people erased by paperwork. She lives in Porto with her sister's family and a dog named Manifesto.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A sleepless night in Lisbon establishes his rituals of erasure: cash, burner phones, no photographs. A call from an old handler warns him someone is querying archives under his birth name. The emotional beat is the ache of belonging to no one.

chapters.title: Flight 409
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He notices a Lisbon-to-Geneva flight blinking out of public trackers mid-air — a skill from his old life. When he pulls the manifest through a dead drop, one name stops him cold. The beat is dread sharpening into recognition.

chapters.title: The Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The manifest lists Ilse Brandt, the defector whose testimony could expose the agency's fabrication of the 'incident.' Edmund realizes whoever erased the flight wants her delivered — or dead — quietly. Beat: the past reaching through the present.

chapters.title: Tarmac Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The plane lands at a closed military strip outside Faro. Ilse, carrying a drive sewn into her coat, slips away during a staged 'customs delay,' sensing the ground crew aren't customs at all. Beat: cold competence masking terror.

chapters.title: Old Debt
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He contacts Tomas, the journalist who once gave him a new name, and asks for the network's help — a debt Tomas says is already spent. Tomas agrees anyway. Beat: gratitude tangled with guilt.

chapters.title: The Fixer
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Marek Voss, the agency's fixer, arrives in Lisbon with a list of four names — all Edmund's — and orders to retrieve Brandt before the summit. He is patient, courteous, and utterly without mercy. Beat: quiet menace.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Edmund and Ilse's POV, alternating. Edmund extracts Ilse from Faro; in the car they trade lies to test each other, then truths. She knows his birth name. Beat: two people with nothing left, recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Drive Holds
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She shows Edmund the evidence: the 'incident' was staged, and the passengers listed on Flight 409 were never meant to exist — including the family who died in Edmund's place. Beat: grief detonated by proof.

chapters.title: The Network Frays
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. One of the journalist network's nodes goes dark; someone inside is feeding Voss. Tomas must choose which safehouses to burn. Beat: paranoia corroding trust.

chapters.title: Madrid Detour
chapters.summary: Edmund and Ilse's POV. A planned handoff in Madrid is a setup; they escape through a train station crowd after Edmund burns his third identity to do it. Beat: adrenaline, then the hollow cost of becoming no one again.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse confesses her suspicion: she was allowed to defect. The agency wants her at Geneva so they can discredit or kill her publicly and bury the evidence forever. Beat: the sickening turn — she is the lure, and Edmund is the intended catch.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Voss captures Tomas and offers a trade: Edmund's surrender for Tomas's life and Ilse's safe passage. Edmund, who has spent the book refusing to belong to anyone, realizes how much he now does. Beat: the trap of love.

chapters.title: Council of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Edmund, Ilse, and remaining network POV. They plan anyway: go to Geneva, but on their terms, using Voss's certainty that Edmund will come alone. Beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The crossing into Switzerland goes wrong when Voss's people flag the car; Ilse and Edmund separate, and Ilse walks the last miles through vineyards with the drive against her heart. Beat: solitude as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: What Voss Knows
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Interrogating Tomas, Voss reveals he was at the 'incident' too — and that he has spent years erasing it out of loyalty, not belief. Beat: the antagonist as a mirror of what Edmund could have become.

chapters.title: Geneva, Day One
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The summit convenes; Edmund infiltrates as a conference contractor, his fourth name now useless, wearing a fifth he invented that morning. Beat: fragile anonymity, coiled anticipation.

chapters.title: The Handover
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse delivers her testimony to a summit liaison — who is Voss's asset. The evidence is seized; Ilse is taken. Beat: hope collapsing in a single handshake.

chapters.title: Exchange
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The trade happens on a bridge at night: Edmund for Ilse and Tomas. He surrenders the drive — a decoy — and lets himself be taken. Beat: sacrifice as the first free choice he's ever made.

chapters.title: The Room Without Windows
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In custody, Voss offers Edmund his old life back under his real name. Edmund refuses — and reveals the drive's contents already went out through the network's dead-man switch when he was taken. Beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: Everything Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multiple POV, rapid cuts. The evidence floods the summit's screens, the press, and every archive the agency thought it owned. Voss's own erasure orders are among them. Beat: catharsis, chaos, reckoning.

chapters.title: Asset and Debt
chapters.summary: Edmund and Ilse's POV. Voss is taken into custody by his own agency to be erased in turn; Edmund testifies under his birth name, Anya Volkova, reclaiming it in daylight. Beat: identity as a choice, not a hiding place.

chapters.title: A Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, epilogue. Months later, Edmund sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident — in Porto, at Tomas's recovered network's new safehouse, surrounded by people who know every name he's ever worn. Beat: belonging, finally, on his own terms.
